title: Pianist Udell, Willie Jackson and records
summary: Williams discusses Udell, singer-dancer Willie Jackson and whether he learned tunes from records.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: What about Udel? Well he was a nice piano player. I never worked with him. Did he work with bands all along?
No, he worked with him and Willie Jackson I think. He worked together at the Cadillac County, St. Peter Rampart.

That's a singer Willie Jackson you're doing? A dancer and a singer, yeah. He was funny. His records are funny. His records are funny. You heard it? Oh yeah, you never heard it? No. I'm a New Orleans Willie Jackson, Old New Orleans Blues Canyon. I don't know. I don't know.
I don't know. It's John of Columbia.
It's in the... I never heard of that record. Yeah. It's in jazz directory. It should be volume five I think.
Now that's a nice record of Louis Savoy.
Yeah. I like that of Louis Savoy. That's a good one. Did you listen to records to pick up tunes out of the bands?
No, no. I just like to hear them. Yeah, just for your own. Yeah, just for your own. I didn't listen to them to play behind them.
